name: RNA Transcription, Post-Transcriptional Processing, and Spliceosome Defects

reference.source: Medical Biochemistry 5th ed / Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd ed
clinicalPearls: RNA polymerase II is selectively and lethally inhibited by alpha-amanitin from Amanita phalloides
Eukaryotic pre-mRNA processing requires 5'-capping (7-methylguanosine), 3'-polyadenylation, and intron splicing
Spliceosome assembly utilizes U1-U6 snRNPs recognizing consensus GU (5'-donor) and AG (3'-acceptor) splice junctions
Anti-Smith (Sm) antibodies in systemic lupus erythematosus specifically target snRNP core proteins
Antisense oligonucleotides (nusinersen) modulate splicing to promote exon inclusion in spinal muscular atrophy
reference.pathophysiology: Eukaryotic transcription requires assembly of pre-initiation complexes at core promoter elements. Following synthesis by RNA polymerase II, nascent transcripts undergo capping, polyadenylation, and spliceosomal removal of non-coding introns. Point mutations within donor or acceptor splice sites disrupt normal exon joining, generating aberrant frame-shifted proteins or premature stop codons as observed in beta-thalassemia.
additionalDifferentials: Systemic lupus erythematosus (autoantibodies to spliceosomal snRNPs)
Spinal muscular atrophy (SMN2 alternative splicing defect)
additionalInvestigations: RT-PCR and cDNA sequencing for aberrant splice junction transcript identification
Anti-Smith (Sm) and anti-U1-RNP antibody titers via ELISA or immunoblotting
Targeted gene sequencing for splice-site donor (GU) and acceptor (AG) mutations
Northern blot or RNA-seq for quantitative transcript isoform profiling
